title: Dot Plots, Stem-and-Leaf Plots, Histograms and Box Plots
seo_title: Grade 6 Dot Plots, Histograms and Box Plots Worksheets (TEKS 6.12A, 6.13A, STAAR)
short_title: Dot Plots, Histograms and Box Plots
standard_text: 6.12A represent numeric data graphically, including dot plots, stem-and-leaf plots, histograms, and box plots; 6.13A interpret numeric data summarized in dot plots, stem-and-leaf plots, histograms, and box plots
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 data worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.12A and 6.13A: read dot plots, stem-and-leaf plots, histograms and box plots, quartiles, range and IQR. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A box plot splits the data into four quarters of about 25% each.
key_sub: Histogram bars count values in intervals. IQR = Q3 − Q1.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A dot plot and a stem-and-leaf plot show every data value.
  • A histogram groups numbers into equal intervals. Each bar shows how many values are in an interval, not the values themselves.
  • A box plot shows the five-number summary: minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum.
  • Each part of a box plot holds about 25% of the data. The box is the middle 50%; its length is the IQR.

Examples

Example

Box plot: 12, 18, 25, 31, 40

Median = 25

IQR = 31 − 18

Answer: 13

Example

Histogram bars 3, 7, 5 for 0–9, 10–19, 20–29

Values 10 or more: 7 + 5

Answer: 12

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading a histogram bar as one valueA bar counts all the values in its interval.
Thinking the middle of the box is always the medianLook for the line inside the box.
Using the range instead of the IQRIQR = Q3 − Q1, the length of the box.

faq.a: Represent numeric data graphically, including dot plots, stem-and-leaf plots, histograms and box plots.
Interpret numeric data summarized in dot plots, stem-and-leaf plots, histograms and box plots.

faq.q: Can you find the mean from a box plot?
faq.a: No. A box plot shows only the five-number summary, not every value.

faq.q: Why can a long whisker still hold 25% of the data?
faq.a: The values in that quarter are spread out, but there are just as many as in each other quarter.

items.q: A class survey asked 12 students how many books they read last month. How many students are shown on the dot plot?
items.e: Each X is one student. Add the X's in every column: 3 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 12.

items.q: The dot plot shows the goals Mia's soccer team scored in 9 games. What is the mode of the data?
items.e: The tallest stack of X's is above 3, so the mode is 3. (The stack has 5 X's, but the mode is the value, not the count.)

items.q: The dot plot shows how many hours each of 12 band members practiced last week. What is the range of the data?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 2 and the X farthest to the right is at 6. Range = 6 − 2 = 4. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: In a class, 10 students took a 10-point quiz. The dot plot shows their scores. What is the median of the data?
items.e: There are 10 X's. The two middle X's are the 5th and 6th from the left. Both are above 7, so the median is 7.

items.q: In a survey, 9 students counted the pets they have at home. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 0 × 1 + 1 × 4 + 2 × 1 + 3 × 1 + 4 × 1 + 5 × 1 = 18. There are 9 X's, so divide by 9: 18 ÷ 9 = 2.

items.q: The dot plot shows how many runs a softball team scored in each of 12 games. What is the mode of the data?
items.e: The tallest stack of X's is above 2, so the mode is 2. (The stack has 4 X's, but the mode is the value, not the count.)

items.q: In a survey, 14 students recorded how many hours they slept last night. What is the median of the data?
items.e: There are 14 X's. The two middle X's are the 7th and 8th from the left. Both are above 8, so the median is 8.

items.q: In a class, 12 students counted the letters in their first names. What is the range of the data?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 5 and the X farthest to the right is at 8. Range = 8 − 5 = 3. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: A class survey asked 12 students how many books they read last month. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 1 × 2 + 2 × 4 + 4 × 2 + 5 × 1 + 6 × 2 + 7 × 1 = 42. There are 12 X's, so divide by 12: 42 ÷ 12 = 3.5.

items.q: The dot plot shows the goals Sofia's soccer team scored in 9 games. How many games are shown on the dot plot?
items.e: Each X is one game. Add the X's in every column: 1 + 2 + 4 + 1 + 1 = 9.

items.q: The dot plot shows how many hours each of 13 band members practiced last week. What is the median of the data?
items.e: There are 13 X's. The median is the 7th X when you count from the left. It is above 5, so the median is 5.

items.q: In a class, 11 students took a 10-point quiz. The dot plot shows their scores. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 3 × 1 + 4 × 2 + 5 × 2 + 7 × 4 + 8 × 1 + 9 × 1 = 66. There are 11 X's, so divide by 11: 66 ÷ 11 = 6.

items.q: In a survey, 14 students counted the pets they have at home. What is the range of the data?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 2 and the X farthest to the right is at 5. Range = 5 − 2 = 3. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: The dot plot shows how many runs a softball team scored in each of 11 games. What is the mode of the data?
items.e: The tallest stack of X's is above 4, so the mode is 4. (The stack has 3 X's, but the mode is the value, not the count.)

items.q: In a survey, 9 students recorded how many hours they slept last night. What is the median of the data?
items.e: There are 9 X's. The median is the 5th X when you count from the left. It is above 9, so the median is 9.

items.q: In a class, 11 students counted the letters in their first names. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 4 × 2 + 5 × 4 + 7 × 3 + 8 × 1 + 9 × 1 = 66. There are 11 X's, so divide by 11: 66 ÷ 11 = 6.

items.q: A class survey asked 10 students how many books they read last month. What is the range of the data?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 0 and the X farthest to the right is at 5. Range = 5 − 0 = 5. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: The dot plot shows the goals Lucia's soccer team scored in 14 games. What is the median of the data?
items.e: There are 14 X's. The two middle X's are the 7th and 8th from the left. Both are above 4, so the median is 4.

items.q: The dot plot shows how many hours each of 9 band members practiced last week. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 2 × 1 + 3 × 4 + 5 × 2 + 6 × 2 = 36. There are 9 X's, so divide by 9: 36 ÷ 9 = 4.

items.q: In a class, 10 students took a 10-point quiz. The dot plot shows their scores. What is the mean of the data?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's and add: 4 × 1 + 6 × 3 + 7 × 5 + 8 × 1 = 65. There are 10 X's, so divide by 10: 65 ÷ 10 = 6.5.
